title: Trim to Balanced Brackets
statement:
The string s contains lowercase letters and the brackets ( and ). Delete the fewest possible brackets so that the rest is balanced: every ( is closed by a later ), and every ) closes an earlier (.

Return the resulting string. Letters are never deleted, and the remaining characters keep their order.

Often several strings need the same smallest number of deletions. Any of them is accepted.

examples.why: The second ) has nothing to close and the last ( is never closed. Two deletions; "k(ey)s" is equally correct.
One of each, so the counts match, but the ) comes first and the ( has nothing after it. Both must go.
Only at the end of the string do you learn that one ( stayed open. Deleting either of the two openers works: "a(bc)d" is also accepted.

constraints: s contains lowercase English letters, ( and )
hints: Which closing brackets can never be kept, no matter what else you delete?
Scan left to right with a stack of indices of unmatched openers. A ) with an empty stack must be deleted. What is left on the stack when the scan ends?
Delete exactly the stray ) found during the scan and the ( indices still on the stack. Each of those has no partner, and everything else is matched, so nothing else needs to go.

explain.intuition:
Match brackets greedily, the way an HTML parser pairs tags: each ) closes the most recent open (. Two kinds of bracket fail. A ) that arrives when nothing is open can never be closed by anything, so it must go. An ( still open at the end has no partner after it, so it must go too.

Those are also the only deletions needed: every other bracket was matched, so the rest is balanced. And you cannot do with fewer, because each stray bracket has no possible partner in any trimmed version. A stack of the indices of open ( tracks the matching; at the end it holds exactly the leftover openers.
steps: Copy s into an array of characters and create a stack of indices.
For ), pop if the stack is not empty; otherwise mark this position for deletion.
After the scan, mark every index still on the stack for deletion.
Join the characters that are not marked.
pitfalls: Only removing stray ) and forgetting the openers that are still open at the end, as in a(b(c)d.
Building the result with repeated string concatenation or deleting characters one at a time from a string, which can turn the whole thing into O(n²).
Treating )( as fine because the counts match. Order matters.

solutions.title: Stack of open indices
solutions.idea: Match each ) with the latest open (. Delete the ) that find nothing and the ( still open at the end.

solutions.title: Two passes with a counter
solutions.idea: Left to right, drop each ) that would make the depth negative. The result has only extra (; right to left, drop the ( that would make the mirrored depth negative.

followups: Return every distinct string that needs the minimum number of deletions. Why does this need a search instead of one pass?
Return only the number of deletions, using O(1) extra space.
